text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today despite a sharp rally over the past two weeks, as crude oil prices pulled back modestly and refinery operations remained steady at near-capacity levels. The small decline likely reflects profit-taking after the stock gained 6.8% since early September, when geopolitical tensions (Iran conflict, Ukraine energy attacks, Saudi pipeline shutdown) pushed oil prices above $100 a barrel and diesel to record highs.

The underlying conditions for a refiner remain supportive: U.S. crude sits at $97.26 and global crude at $109.51, refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, and storage levels across oil and products are tight—all factors that typically strengthen refining margins. However, the recent political developments (Trump's reported negotiations to halt Ukraine attacks on Russian energy) introduce uncertainty about whether crude supply pressures will ease, which could weigh on the stock near term.
